name: The Foxhole

stars.name: Thorn
stars.notes: An ancient orange star at the far edge of settled space. Its dim, steady light has watched over a world that learned to fight in the shadows. The locals say Thorn never blinks—and neither do they.

planets.name: Tripwire
planets.notes: Inner rocky world seeded with proximity sensors and automated weapons by the guerrillas. Any vessel approaching the inner system on a standard trajectory receives an unpleasant welcome.

planets.name: Briarwood
planets.notes: A densely forested world with 600,000 inhabitants who have turned their planet into a fortress. The canopy hides settlements, the caves hide arsenals, and the population has been fighting the Drakon Mandate's occupation forces for eight years with no intention of stopping.

planets.name: Deadfall
planets.notes: Airless world whose subsurface tunnel networks serve as guerrilla supply caches. The Drakon Mandate has raided these caches repeatedly, but the tunnel system is too extensive to fully clear.

planets.name: Blackthorn
planets.notes: A dark, ringed gas giant. The Drakon Mandate maintains a fuel depot and patrol base among its moons, but guerrilla raiders have destroyed the depot twice, forcing costly rebuilds.

anomalies.name: The Canopy
anomalies.notes: Briarwood's native forest emits a complex bioelectric field that interferes with orbital sensor sweeps. The Drakon Mandate cannot reliably distinguish human settlements from natural biomass concentrations, making precision strikes nearly impossible.

anomalies.name: Thornfield Mines
anomalies.location: Standard approach vectors to Briarwood orbit
anomalies.notes: The guerrillas have seeded the most common orbital insertion paths with improvised mines—repurposed industrial charges, salvaged warheads, and even pressurized fuel canisters. The fields are irregular, undocumented, and lethal.

stations.name: Mandate Forward Base
stations.notes: The Drakon Mandate's orbital command post for counterinsurgency operations. Has been hit by improvised kinetic weapons launched from the surface three times. The crew rotation rate is the highest in the Mandate military—no one wants to stay.

stations.name: The Roots
stations.location: Deep cave network beneath Briarwood's southern continent
stations.notes: The guerrilla leadership's headquarters, buried under kilometers of rock and forest. Its location is one of the most closely guarded secrets on Briarwood. The Mandate has offered a staggering bounty for its coordinates.

faction_control.primary: Contested — Drakon Mandate (occupying force) / Briarwood Resistance
faction_control.notes: The Drakon Mandate invaded eight years ago and has never achieved control. They hold orbit and a handful of fortified surface bases; the Briarwood Resistance holds everything else. The forest fights for the guerrillas—its bioelectric interference defeats sensors, its density defeats armor, and its people have turned every trail, every clearing, every cave into a potential ambush site.

history: Briarwood was colonized in 2604 by settlers who specifically chose its remote location and dense forest for privacy. For over a century, the colony was effectively invisible—too far from major routes, too small, and too obscure to attract attention.

The Drakon Mandate's expansion into the Bramble Reach in 2718 brought unwanted contact. When Briarwood refused to submit to Mandate governance, a marine division was deployed for what commanders estimated would be a three-week pacification campaign. Eight years later, the campaign continues.

The Briarwood Resistance has become a symbol of asymmetric defiance across the sector. Their tactics—improvised weapons, tunnel networks, exploitation of the forest's natural sensor interference—have been studied and replicated by resistance movements on other Mandate-occupied worlds. The Mandate has rotated six different commanders through the system, each promising to end the insurgency. None has succeeded.
description: The Foxhole is a system that looks like nothing from the outside: a dim orange star, four unremarkable worlds, no significant resources. This appearance is its first defense. Briarwood, the sole inhabited planet, is a world of dense primeval forest whose canopy hides 600,000 people who have spent eight years proving that occupation is not the same as control. The Drakon Mandate holds the orbitals and a few fortified bases; the guerrillas hold the forest, the caves, and the will of the population.

The Mandate's counterinsurgency campaign is a study in frustration. Briarwood's native forest generates bioelectric interference that blinds orbital sensors, making it impossible to distinguish settlements from natural biomass. Ground operations in the dense forest favor the defenders, who know every trail and have had eight years to prepare ambush sites, tunnel networks, and improvised weapon caches. The Mandate's technological superiority is neutralized by terrain, and their troop morale suffers accordingly—the orbital forward base has the highest crew rotation rate in the Mandate military.

For outsiders willing to navigate minefields and evade Mandate patrols, The Foxhole offers a peculiar market. The resistance needs off-world supplies—medical equipment, communications gear, weapons components that cannot be fabricated from forest materials. They pay in rare hardwoods, bioactive compounds harvested from Briarwood's unique ecology, and intelligence on Mandate force dispositions. The Mandate, meanwhile, pays bounties for guerrilla intelligence and hires deniable contractors for operations too dirty for uniformed troops. And across the sector, other resistance movements watch Briarwood as proof that empires can bleed.
